notes:
Account summary
- Inbound after reading Redwood latency/$ benchmark report + interactive table. Very cost-sensitive team; primary motivation is reducing $/request while keeping p95 stable.
- Quote from inbound form: "Your latency/$ chart is the first one that matches what our CFO actually cares about. We need guidance on caching/batching so we don’t accidentally game numbers in prod."

What they build / workload
- AI-native workflow automation product (end users trigger multi-step LLM flows).
- Mix: (1) support-agent chat (streaming), (2) internal summarization jobs (non-streaming), (3) embeddings for doc search.
- Traffic pattern: spiky during business hours; background summarization runs overnight.

Key requirements (current understanding)
- Latency: p50 < 700ms, p95 < 1500ms for chat (North America). They also care about EU performance for a subset of customers.
- Cost: explicit mandate to cut inference spend 25–35% vs current provider; wants a clear path to lowering $/1M tokens (and not just a one-off benchmark).
- Reliability: wants safe fallback strategy if a model/region is saturated ("we can degrade but can’t go dark").
- Controls: wants spend guardrails (quotas), plus alerts that map usage -> estimated dollars.

Benchmark-specific questions they asked (verbatim/paraphrase)
- "Were the published numbers with caching on or off?"
- "How does continuous batching affect p95 at real concurrency?"
- "If our prompts are highly personalized, is prefix/KV caching still worth it?"
- "Can we reproduce your latency/$ locally or in our own VPC?"

What we told them (safe talk track)
- Explained methodology at a high level and pointed to the public methodology summary; emphasized workload dependence and that results are directional, not a guarantee for every prompt distribution.
- Clarified the knobs we can tune in a PoC: max batch latency, target concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming routes, caching policies (prefix/KV) with explicit hit-rate monitoring.
- Positioned Redwood Optimize as the place we provide concrete recommendations + regression monitoring once they have traces.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-07-11: Inbound via benchmark landing page CTA; asked for "caching/batching best practices" and "replication steps".
- 2025-07-14: SDR qualification (Grace O’Connor). Confirmed they are evaluating alternatives this quarter; budget owner is Head of Eng + Finance partner.
- 2025-07-18: Eval kickoff w/ Stephanie + Markus. Shared high-level architecture + current provider costs (rough numbers, not audited). They flagged that streaming stability matters more than raw tokens/sec.
- 2025-07-22: OrbitAI requested written guidance: recommended default batching/caching settings by workload (chat vs batch jobs) + how to measure cache hit rate.
- 2025-07-24: Perf review. Markus walked through how Redwood handles continuous batching, queueing, and tail latency; agreed to run a small A/B: caching on/off, two batch windows.

POC plan (draft)
- Phase 1 (Hosted API): replicate their top 3 flows using Redwood SDK; capture p50/p95, throughput, $/1M tokens, and latency/$.
- Phase 2 (Tuning): apply batching + caching changes; compare cost deltas while watching p95 and output quality.
- Phase 3 (Scale / Dedicated): if they need more predictable throughput during spikes, evaluate Dedicated pool sizing.

Risks / watchouts
- Their prompts may have low cacheability due to per-user context injection; we should set expectations that caching benefits depend on prefix reuse and request similarity.
- They have both streaming and batch workloads; we need to avoid a single setting that optimizes cost but hurts UX on chat.

Open questions
- Which models are they currently using (and why)? They were vague: "mix of frontier + an open model endpoint".
- EU requirement: do they need data residency or just low latency in EU? (they said "we have customers in Germany" but didn’t confirm residency constraints).

Internal guidance
- Keep the story anchored on production economics + controllability: show how to measure, tune, and monitor—do not over-claim that benchmark numbers will match their app.
- If they push hard on "just tell us the magic caching settings," redirect to: we’ll recommend based on their measured prefill/decode distribution + concurrency + cache hit rate, then lock it into guardrails.
